text:
guise

 
 
 
 

A component library for gpui — the
GPU-accelerated Rust UI framework that powers Zed.

 guise gives gpui a batteries-included component layer: a themed palette,
sizing tokens, 130+ composable components, a reactive state layer with two-way
bindings, an animation system with keyframes and a scrubbable playhead, and the
full Lucide icon set embedded as the default icons — no
asset pipeline needed.

 Tailor is the other half: a drag-and-drop builder that lays these
same components out on a canvas and exports idiomatic Rust. Write the interface
or draw it — either way you end up with the same components. It is its own
project, and consumes this library from crates.io like anyone else.

 

 Tailor — the visual interface builder

 Tailor is a drag-and-drop interface builder for gpui and guise,
shaped like Interface Builder and Android Studio's layout editor. Lay out a
screen from real components, wire the state and the actions, and export
idiomatic Rust that has no dependency on Tailor left in it.

Its canvas is not a drawing of your interface — a Button on it is a real
 guise::Button , reading the same theme. Every release attaches
a signed Tailor.dmg , with an MCP server in the bundle so an agent can build a
screen with no window open.

It lived in this repository through 1.6.0 and moved out after; its
documentation moved with it.

 Documentation

Full docs live in docs/ (also rendered at
wess.github.io/guise):

- Tutorial — build a complete app step by step (web version)
- App walkthrough — a project tracker wired the way a real guise app fits together
- Motion tutorial — one animated panel, nine chapters (web version)
- Getting started · Theming · Component model
- Components: Buttons · Icons · Inputs · Dates & times · File handling · Typography · Layout · Panels · Feedback · Data · Charts · GPU View · Video · Editor · Markdown editor · AI · Overlays · Navigation
- Systems: Flex layout · Macros · Motion & transitions · Drag & drop · Reactive state · Software update · Settings · DevTools · Window menu & chrome · Architecture · Size & performance
- Tailor lives at github.com/wess/tailor, documentation included
- Releasing · Changelog

 Workspace

- crates/guise — the component library, published as guise-ui . The only
 crate here that reaches crates.io.
- crates/gallery — a live showcase of every component
 ( cargo run -p gallery ).
- site/ — the Bun generator that renders docs/ into the website.

 cargo package -p guise-ui --list is the proof that the crate carries the
library and nothing else — it depends on nothing but gpui and std.

 How guise compares

Two other component libraries target gpui:
gpui-component (shadcn-flavored,
backs Longbridge Pro) and
adabraka-ui. A quick orientation, as
of July 2026:

 guise gpui-component adabraka-ui 
 --- --- --- --- 
 Design language open-color palette + token scales shadcn/ui shadcn/ui 
 Components 130+ 60+ 140 
 Visual builder Tailor — — 
 Reactive layer Signal / Binding / lenses, reactive Form — (entities + subscriptions) — 
 Icons all 1,991 Lucide glyphs as an embedded font, zero setup 99 Lucide SVGs via an assets crate 1,600 SVGs, copied into your app manually 
 Theming open-color palette, JSON theme files, 6 presets, per-slot overrides 140 tokens, JSON themes with hot reload, 22 presets 19 presets, theme behind a global Mutex 
 Code editor 10-language highlighter + diagnostics API tree-sitter ( 35 languages) + LSP client tree-sitter (22 languages) 
 Docking / panels PaneGroup splits-with-tabs + layout persistence DockArea + floating Tiles + serialization resizable/split panels 
 Charts 6 types with axes, legends, hover 6 types incl. candlestick & Sankey on a plot framework 11 types 
 Motion easing curves, spring physics, exit animations basic easing large effects library 
 Drag & drop typed payloads, sortable lists panel docking draggable + sortable 
 Date/time pickers yes yes (incl. range presets) yes 
 Tests 640+ incl. gpui entity harness 580 incl. render tests minimal 
 gpui dependency crates.io releases crates.io releases; dev tracks zed main a custom gpui fork 
 License MIT Apache-2.0 MIT 

Reach for guise if you want chainable builders, SwiftUI-style two-way
bindings, and icons that just work with zero asset setup. gpui-component 
is the bigger ecosystem — a production code editor with LSP, a full dock
system, and a WASM story. adabraka-ui ships the largest effects/animation
collection.

 Theme

Install a theme once at startup; every component reads it from the gpui global:

 

The theme carries the full open-color
palette (14 colors × 10 shades), xs..xl scales for spacing, radius and font size, and scheme-aware semantic
colors ( body , surface , text , dimmed , border , plus success /
 warning / danger / info feedback accents). Themes also load from flat
JSON files — Theme::from json(source) — with no serde dependency.

 CSS-style colors

Write colors the CSS way — hex, rgb / rgba , hsl / hsla , or named — with the
 color! macro (compile-time) or css(..) (runtime strings). Both produce a
gpui Hsla , usable in .bg(..) / .text color(..) , in any component .color(..) ,
and in the theme with overrides:

 

 color! takes rgb(..) / rgba(..) / hsl(..) / hsla(..) /named tokens or a CSS
string (hex must be a string — 228be6 isn't a Rust token). Component
 .color(..) accepts a palette ColorName or an explicit color (the
 ColorValue type) and derives variant shades from a single custom color. See
Theming.

intro.html:
A component library for gpui — the GPU-accelerated Rust UI framework that powers Zed.

guise gives gpui a batteries-included component layer: a themed palette, sizing tokens, 130+ composable components, a reactive state layer with two-way bindings, an animation system with keyframes and a scrubbable playhead, and the full Lucide icon set embedded as the default icons — no asset pipeline needed.

Tailor is the other half: a drag-and-drop builder that lays these same components out on a canvas and exports idiomatic Rust. Write the interface or draw it — either way you end up with the same components. It is its own project, and consumes this library from crates.io like anyone else.

use guise::prelude::*;

Stack::new()
    .gap(Size::Md)
    .child(Title::new("Welcome").order(1))
    .child(
        Button::new("save", "Save changes")
            .variant(Variant::Filled)
            .color(ColorName::Blue)
            .on_click(|_, window, cx| { /* ... */ }),
    )

install.title: Installation
install.html:
guise builds against crates.io gpui 0.2.2 — no git pins, no patch sections:

[dependencies]
guise-ui = "1.5"
gpui = "0.2.2"

The crate is named guise-ui (the guise name was taken on crates.io), but its library is named guise — so you still write use guise::prelude::*;.

Pinning via git works too:

guise-ui = { git = "https://github.com/wess/guise", tag = "v1.6.0" }
